system_note: What was billed: Principal A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae) with R65.21 (severe sepsis/septic shock) and multiple MCC/CC secondary diagnoses including J96.01, J80, J95.851 (VAP, POA=N flagged CC on the claim), N17.9, plus status codes Z99.11 and Z99.2. Procedures for intubation, tracheostomy, prolonged ventilation (>96 hrs) and renal replacement are billed. What the record documents (selected, line-referenced evidence): - Sepsis/septic shock present on arrival with lactate 5.1 and vasopressors/urgent intubation: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, 2026-04-04, pp.312-580: "In the ED the patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated." (supports A40.3/R65.21, POA=Y) - Organism identified on admission cultures: Infectious Diseases Consultation, Chart Notes, 2026-04-09, pp.137-489: "Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP. Admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (now cleared); BAL pending." (supports organism-specific sepsis A40.3 and pneumonia due to S. pneumoniae) - ARDS / respiratory failure documented with low P/F ratios and ARDS-directed management: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, 2026-04-04, pp.312-580: active problems include "Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), moderate-severe" and ventilator orders listing ARDSnet; Respiratory Therapy Note, Chart Notes, 2026-04-16, p.386 documents ventilator settings (PEEP 12, FiO2 75%) and P/F consistent with moderate-severe hypoxemia (supports J80 and J96.01). - VAP onset during hospitalization with Pseudomonas identified and treated: Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, 2026-04-09, p.137: "Interval: fever recrudescence, rising WBC, purulent secretions and new right infiltrate - VAP suspected; antimicrobials broadened per ID"; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp.923-924: "resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas) ... treated with a targeted course of cefepime after bronchoscopy." (supports J95.851 POA=N and organism specification B96.5) - AKI requiring RRT documented then renal recovery / dialysis discontinued: Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, 2026-04-06, p.123: "Oliguric AKI ... meeting criteria for renal replacement therapy." Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp.923-924: "acute kidney injury with renal recovery, hemodialysis discontinued." (supports N17.9 during encounter; documents dialysis was later discontinued) - Right internal jugular catheter-associated DVT documented: Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, 2026-04-25, p.330: "Venous Duplex Ultrasound, Right Upper Extremity: Right internal jugular deep vein thrombosis (catheter-associated)." (supports right IJ DVT / T82.818A) Audit findings and rationale tied to policy & record: 1) J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia) - presence and POA: The chart contains explicit provider documentation diagnosing VAP (ID consult and progress notes) with onset on hospital day ~6 and targeted therapy for Pseudomonas; POA=N is correct (VAP developed >48h after intubation). However, policy designates J95.851 as an MCC (see Policy Documents/DRG/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx). The claim's J95.851 line is flagged only as CC - this is a severity-tier miscoding. Evidence: policy header "J95.851 - Ventilator associated pneumonia [MCC]" (Policy Documents/DRG/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx) vs. ID/Critical Care notes documenting VAP and Pseudomonas (Infectious Diseases Consultation; Critical Care Progress Note). Correction: J95.851 should be MCC on the claim (not CC). 2) I82.C12 (Acute embolism/thrombosis of left internal jugular vein) - laterality / code not supported: Imaging and progress notes document a right internal jugular DVT ("Right internal jugular deep vein thrombosis (catheter-associated)." Critical Care Progress Note, 2026-04-25). The claim lists a left-sided I82.C12; that contradicts the record. The hospital problem list and billing summary use a catheter-associated IJ DVT (T82.818A). Action: replace I82.C12 with the clinically documented code for right IJ catheter-associated DVT (T82.818A as present in the problem list / billing summary) or I82.C11 if facility coding prefers an anatomic I82.* format - but the chart-provided coded problem list uses T82.818A. This is a diagnosis-code mismatch (remove I82.C12; add T82.818A). 3) Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis) - status-code left active after resolution: Nephrology and discharge notes document initiation of RRT during the encounter followed by renal recovery and discontinuation of hemodialysis prior to transfer/discharge (Discharge / Transfer Summary: "hemodialysis discontinued"). A dependence-on-dialysis status code (Z99.2) is inappropriate to persist at final billing when the record documents renal recovery and dialysis discontinuation. Action: remove Z99.2 from the final diagnosis set (AKI and procedure codes documenting interim RRT remain appropriate). 4) Principal diagnosis sequencing: A40.3 (sepsis due to S. pneumoniae) listed as principal is supported by provider documentation and positive admission blood cultures attributing sepsis to Streptococcus pneumoniae (Infectious Diseases Consultation and H&P). R65.21 is correctly present as an additional severe sepsis/septic shock code. Keep A40.3 as principal. 5) Other diagnoses and procedures (J96.01, J80, N17.9, B96.5, E11.65, J44.9, I48.91, F05, G72.81, Z99.11, procedures for intubation/trach/ventilation/CRRT/PEG) are supported by the cited clinical documentation (H&P, consults, RT notes, nephrology, discharge summary). No removal of those codes is recommended. Summary correction actions applied to the whole claim (complete corrected lists provided below). Citations: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, pp.312-580; Infectious Diseases Consultation, Chart Notes, pp.137-489; Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, 2026-04-09 p.137 & 2026-04-25 p.330; Nephrology Consultation, Chart Notes, 2026-04-06 p.123; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp.923-924; Policy Documents/DRG/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx (J95.851 - MCC).
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical Coding Audit - Admission Claim MR_09 Dear Provider / Health Information Management Team, We audited the inpatient claim MR_09 (admit 2026-04-04) for completeness and accuracy of diagnostic and procedure coding against the medical record and the applicable DRG coding policy guidance. Our review used the treating clinicians' documentation, consult notes, imaging and laboratory data, and the applicable DRG validation rules. Finding: We identified multiple coding errors requiring correction. 1) J95.851 - Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP): Supported by the record (ID consult and ICU progress notes document VAP developing on hospital day ~6 with Pseudomonas isolated and targeted therapy). Per the DRG VAP policy (Policy Documents/DRG/Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx), J95.851 is an MCC. On the submitted claim J95.851 was marked as a CC-level condition; this understates the severity and must be corrected to MCC. POA=N is correct. 2) I82.C12 - Acute embolism/thrombosis of left internal jugular vein: The medical record documents a right internal jugular catheter-associated DVT (Venous Duplex: "Right internal jugular deep vein thrombosis (catheter-associated)", Critical Care Progress Note 2026-04-25). The billed left-sided I82.C12 does not match the documented laterality or the facility problem list (which lists a catheter-associated IJ DVT). The correct diagnosis code should reflect the documented right IJ catheter-associated DVT (the chart's problem list/billing summary uses T82.818A). Replace I82.C12 with the code supported by the imaging and problem list documentation. 3) Z99.2 - Dependence on renal dialysis: Nephrology consultation and the discharge summary document that renal replacement therapy (CRRT then intermittent HD) was initiated during the hospitalization for AKI but renal function recovered and hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer/discharge (Discharge / Transfer Summary). Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) indicates ongoing dialysis dependence and is not supported at discharge. Remove Z99.2 from the final code set. Continue to report the acute kidney injury (N17.9) and the procedure codes for RRT/dialysis during the encounter. 4) Principal diagnosis sequencing: The record supports sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae with septic shock (positive admission blood cultures and treating provider documentation). A40.3 as the principal diagnosis with R65.21 as an additional severe sepsis/septic shock code is supported and should remain sequenced as billed. Correction enacted: We adjusted the claim-level diagnosis set to (a) correct laterality for the catheter-associated IJ DVT per the chart, (b) remove the dialysis-dependence status code that resolved before discharge, and (c) update the VAP severity to MCC. All other coded diagnoses and procedures were verified as supported and retained. If you dispute the above corrections or have additional documentation (e.g., a physician attestation that dialysis dependence was chronic and ongoing at discharge, or that the thrombus was left-sided), please provide it so we may re-evaluate. Attached are the exact chart excerpts and policy citations used in our determination. Sincerely, Clinical Coding Audit Team
